text:
Peyton Krebs came to Buffalo in the Jack Eichel trade almost five years ago, and according to the Buffalo News he's closing in on his 400th NHL game. He's become exactly what that trade's skeptics doubted he would: a dependable middle-six forward who plays hard (41 hits) and moves the puck.

This season the line is lopsided: one goal and nine assists in 21 games. His shooting is at 6.7% on just 15 shots, and his chances, 2.93 expected goals, say he should have two or three more goals. He's had six points in his last ten, with his ice time rising to 15:26.

Is it real? At five-on-five the Sabres are dead even with him on or off the ice, which is fine for a third-line center but not more. Evolving-Hockey liked his 2025-26, 1.5 wins and 93rd among forwards, while warning that his results ran far ahead of his chances (0.3 expected wins). That fits what we see now: a useful player whose ceiling is a 40-point season, which is about where our projection has him.
headline: Krebs is setting up, not scoring
